[ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887) supports a learnable residual scalar initialized exactly to zero: z=h+αr, α=0. Applied here, this preserves baseline features and scores at initialization if the backbone and scoring path remain identical. However, z=LN(h+0·r)=LN(h), which generally differs from h: an added outer LayerNorm breaks exact preservation, even with affine parameters γ=1, β=0. Preserve the baseline by inserting the branch before its existing final normalization, retaining that normalization’s parameters and epsilon, or by omitting the added outer normalization.

Gradient implications follow directly: for g=σ(a), dg/da=g(1−g); initializing g=0.01 gives derivative 0.0099, versus 0.25 at g=0.5. A very negative bias therefore makes the residual small while slowing gate learning; finite sigmoid logits never yield exact zero. With an unconstrained zero-initialized α, the gate can receive a nonzero gradient immediately, although branch-exclusive parameters receive zero gradient initially. Avoid simultaneously zeroing the gate and branch output, which can stall both. These are mathematical implications; [GTrXL](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.06764) provides related evidence for identity-favoring gated initialization, rather than evidence specific to this recommender.

Normalization deserves its own control: the [SASRec PyTorch maintainer’s experiments](https://github.com/pmixer/SASRec.pytorch/blob/main/Result_Norm.md) report recommendation changes from normalization placement alone. Recommended ablations: untouched baseline; added outer LN with residual disabled; zero-gated residual preserving baseline normalization; full residual plus outer LN. Match backbone initialization, sampling and training seeds; compare initialization logits numerically and monitor gate values and gradients. Pool normalization controls residual scale but cannot make an added outer LN an identity.
